data.description:
## Observation

Closing `fb5f-54fd-96cc-4105` through the MCP server failed the AC precheck
while the same server's read tools reported the criteria satisfied, seconds
apart and against the same ticket:

- `check_ac(fb5f-54fd-96cc-4105)` → `{"verdict":"pass","criteria_count":6,"passed":true}`
- `show_ticket(fb5f-54fd-96cc-4105, field=description)` → description length
  7288, **0** occurrences of `- [ ]`, **6** of `- [x]`, `updated_at`
  `1793509059386284001`
- `transition_ticket(fb5f-54fd-96cc-4105, in_progress → closed)` → exit 1,
  `has unchecked Acceptance Criteria items:` listing all **6** criteria with
  `- [ ]`, quoting the pre-edit text verbatim

The description had been edited (all 6 boxes ticked) through the local CLI in a
worktree; that write was committed and pushed to `origin/tickets`. A local
`rebar show fb5f-54fd-96cc-4105 --field description` in that worktree confirmed
0 unchecked / 6 checked, as did the MCP read above.

Retrying `transition_ticket` reproduced the identical failure, so this is not a
one-shot race that settles on its own.

The same transition then **succeeded on the first attempt** through the local
CLI from a worktree synced to the merged commit.

## Why this matters

The error text instructs the operator to "Resolve each item before closing, then
check the box (edit the description)" — which had already been done, and which
the server's own read path confirmed. An operator following the message has no
remaining action, and the only paths out are `--force` (prohibited for agents)
or discovering the local-CLI workaround. It presents as an unclosable ticket.

The inconsistency is the defect: one MCP server answering a read and a write
from different views of the same ticket. Whichever view is correct, they must
not disagree.

## Hypotheses (unproven)

1. `transition_ticket` shells out to `rebar transition` in a working directory
   whose store clone is behind the one the in-process read tools use. The error
   is prefixed `rebar transition failed (exit 1)`, which is consistent with a
   subprocess, and would explain a stale description surviving a retry.
2. The precheck resolves the description from a pinned plan/claim snapshot
   rather than live ticket state, while `check_ac` reads live state. The ticket
   is `plan_review_phase: execution`, so a snapshot exists.

These predict different fixes, so distinguish them before changing anything.

## Reproduction

1. Pick a ticket with unchecked AC items whose work is complete.
2. Edit the description through the **local CLI in a worktree**, ticking every
   box; confirm the write pushed.
3. Call MCP `show_ticket --field description` and `check_ac` — both report the
   ticket as satisfied.
4. Call MCP `transition_ticket` to closed — fails listing the stale unchecked
   items. Retrying does not clear it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The source `transition_ticket`'s AC precheck reads is identified, and
      which of the 2 hypotheses holds is stated with evidence from the code
      path, not inference from the error string.
- [ ] A regression test fails before the fix and passes after: an AC precheck
      invoked through the same entry point `transition_ticket` uses observes a
      description edit that `check_ac` already observes.
- [ ] MCP `check_ac` and MCP `transition_ticket`'s precheck return the same
      verdict for the same ticket at the same moment, for both a satisfied and
      an unsatisfied ticket.
- [ ] If the stale view is a subprocess store clone, the refresh (or the shared
      store handle) is covered by a test that would catch a regression to a
      second clone.
- [ ] `make verify` green.
data.title: MCP transition_ticket AC precheck reads a stale description that check_ac does not
